title: HIV-1 Tat and Heparan Sulfate Proteoglycans Orchestrate the Setup of in Cis and in Trans Cell-Surface Interactions Functional to Lymphocyte Trans-Endothelial Migration.
authors: Urbinati, Chiara; Milanesi, Maria; Lauro, Nicola; Bertelli, Cinzia; David, Guido; D'Ursi, Pasqualina; Rusnati, Marco; Chiodelli, Paola
one_liner_zh: 该文研究HIV-1 Tat蛋白与硫酸肝素蛋白聚糖介导的淋巴细胞-内皮跨内皮迁移互作，含Tat/肝素复合物的分子建模、对接与动力学模拟，属广义蛋白-糖胺聚糖互作而非TF-DNA体系，但结构建模方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA界面研究。
abstract: HIV-1 transactivating factor Tat is released by infected cells. Extracellular Tat homodimerizes and engages several receptors, including integrins, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) and heparan sulfate proteoglycan (HSPG) syndecan-1 expressed on various cells. By means of experimental cell models recapitulating the processes of lymphocyte trans-endothelial migration, here, we demonstrate that upon association with syndecan-1 expressed on lymphocytes, Tat triggers simultaneously the in cis activation of lymphocytes themselves and the in trans activation of endothelial cells (ECs). This "two-way" activation eventually induces lymphocyte adhesion and spreading onto the substrate and vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin reorganization at the EC junctions, with consequent endothelial permeabilization, leading to an increased extravasation of Tat-presenting lymphocytes. By means of a panel of biochemical activation assays and specific synthetic inhibitors, we demonstrate that during the above-mentioned processes, syndecan-1, integrins, FAK, src and ERK(1/2) engagement and activation are needed in the lymphocytes, while VEGFR2, integrin, src and ERK(1/2) are needed in the endothelium. In conclusion, the Tat/syndecan-1 complex plays a central role in orchestrating the setup of the various in cis and in trans multimeric complexes at the EC/lymphocyte interface. Thus, by means of computational molecular modelling, docking and dynamics, we also provide a characterization at an atomic level of the binding modes of the Tat/heparin interaction, with heparin herein used as a structural analogue of the heparan sulfate chains of syndecan-1.
abstract_zh: HIV-1反式激活因子Tat由受感染细胞释放。细胞外Tat同源二聚化并结合多种受体，包括整合素、血管内皮生长因子受体2（VEGFR2）及表达于多种细胞表面的硫酸乙酰肝素蛋白聚糖（HSPG）多配体蛋白聚糖-1（syndecan-1）。通过模拟淋巴细胞跨内皮迁移过程的实验细胞模型，我们在此证明，当Tat与淋巴细胞表面表达的多配体蛋白聚糖-1结合时，同时触发淋巴细胞自身的顺式激活和内皮细胞（ECs）的反式激活。这种“双向”激活最终诱导淋巴细胞粘附并铺展于基质上，以及内皮连接处血管内皮（VE）-钙黏蛋白的重组，导致内皮通透性增加，进而促进携带Tat的淋巴细胞外渗增加。通过一系列生化激活实验和特异性合成抑制剂，我们证明在上述过程中，淋巴细胞内需要多配体蛋白聚糖-1、整合素、FAK、src和ERK(1/2)的参与和激活，而内皮中则需要VEGFR2、整合素、src和ERK(1/2)。总之，Tat/多配体蛋白聚糖-1复合物在协调内皮细胞/淋巴细胞界面处各种顺式和反式多聚体复合物的组装中发挥核心作用。因此，通过计算分子建模、对接和动力学模拟，我们还在原子水平上提供了Tat/肝素相互作用的结合模式表征，其中肝素在此用作多配体蛋白聚糖-1硫酸乙酰肝素链的结构类似物。
